title: Counter-Selector Wave 38: content-addressed checkpoint operation join and hidden predecessor remainder
purpose: Adjudicate the first public same-object checkpoint surface that joins a content-addressed portable package to observed successor operation, while preserving the absence of itemized internal inventory, recipient acknowledgment, complete authority and dependency custody, hidden-predecessor-state freedom, external independent review, and person-level support.

complete_portable_operational_handoff_re: one same object and transition boundary are identified
one versioned content-addressed portable package binds the transferred state
every operational entry is itemized with integrity and semantic role
the incoming recipient acknowledges the exact package inventory and authority state
credentials dependencies access open decisions deadlines and rollback state travel with the package
the destination operates without undeclared predecessor state or hidden environmental borrowing
successor operation is observed from the exact acknowledged package
an external independent verifier reproduces the whole package-to-operation chain

controls.public_label: content-addressed OCI checkpoint image restored after source-container removal

source_records.title: Podman container checkpoint command contract
source_records.artifact_scope: Defines checkpoint export, --create-image as a standard OCI image, transport through registries, rootfs and volume inclusion, runtime constraints, and live-checkpoint consistency limits.

source_records.title: Podman container restore command contract
source_records.artifact_scope: Defines restore from checkpoint images or archives, cross-host import, runtime matching, network, volume, TCP, port, name, and failure options.

source_records.title: Checkpoint image create, remove, restore, and running-state end-to-end test
source_records.artifact_scope: Creates one checkpoint OCI image, verifies checkpoint annotations, removes the source container, restores from the image, and asserts the successor container is running.

source_records.title: Checkpoint image construction and compatibility metadata
source_records.artifact_scope: Builds a scratch image, exports checkpoint state into one tar layer, adds container and host compatibility annotations, and commits the checkpoint image.

source_records.title: Checkpoint image restore dispatch
source_records.artifact_scope: Recognizes a checkpoint image, mounts it, imports exactly one container configuration, and invokes restore.

source_records.title: Checkpoint configuration import and hidden rootfs dependency
source_records.artifact_scope: Reads spec and config, validates selected topology constraints, pulls the original rootfs image if missing, creates the successor container, and enforces restored name and ID.

source_records.title: OCI content descriptor contract
source_records.artifact_scope: Defines digest and size descriptors, content addressability, and independent digest verification for referenced bytes.

source_records.title: OCI image manifest contract
source_records.artifact_scope: Defines content-addressed image configuration and layer descriptors for one portable container image.

source_records.title: Checkpoint image annotations and running-success assertions
source_records.artifact_scope: Verifies original name and runtime annotations, deletes the source container, restores the image, and observes an Up successor without application-specific semantic checks.

components.same_object_identity: The checkpoint preserves the container configuration, CRIU process state, original name, and—unless a new name is requested—the original container ID across source removal and successor creation.
components.package_identity: Podman creates a scratch checkpoint image containing one squashed checkpoint archive layer and compatibility annotations for the source container and host/runtime environment.
components.package_content_addressing: The OCI image manifest binds configuration and layer bytes through digest-and-size descriptors, creating one package-level content identifier.
components.internal_inventory_and_entry_integrity: The layer contains checkpoint artifacts, config and spec dumps, network state, CRIU images, rootfs changes, and optional volume archives, but there is no per-entry manifest or digest ledger; image import copies a fixed list and logs unavailable entries rather than acknowledging an exact inventory.
components.outgoing_and_incoming_roles: The outgoing Podman/CRIU checkpoint role emits the image; the incoming Podman/CRIU restore role imports it and creates the successor container.
components.authority_and_credentials: Container config, runtime annotations, and restore options are present, but no complete operational authority, credential, secret, or recipient-rights ledger is itemized and acknowledged.
components.dependencies_and_access: The restore path pulls the original rootfs image by name when missing and still depends on compatible Podman, OCI runtime, CRIU, kernel, cgroups, storage, network, and volume conditions outside the checkpoint layer.
components.open_decisions_and_deadlines: TCP, volume, rootfs, name, pod, network, and port restore choices remain invocation-time decisions rather than an acknowledged package decision ledger.
components.rollback_safe_decline_and_failure_contai: Runtime incompatibility, missing required config, topology conflicts, and missing CRIU inventory can stop restore; successful restore has no same-package rollback receipt to the removed source container.
components.recipient_or_successor_acknowledgment: The restore runtime accepts enough state to create and run the successor, but neither a human recipient nor the runtime signs or enumerates every package entry, dependency, authority, and open decision.
components.successor_operation_from_package: The exact checkpoint image test removes the original container, restores from that image, and observes the successor in running state with original identity constraints.
components.independent_verification: The implementation and end-to-end tests are public and reproducible inside the originating project; no external institution independently reproduced the exact package-to-operation chain.

positive_findings: One standard OCI image binds the checkpoint package at the configuration-and-layer level through content descriptors.
The source container is removed before restore, so the observed successor is created from the checkpoint image rather than an existing container record.
The restore path preserves the original container name and enforces the original ID unless an explicit rename is requested.
The successor reaches running state from the checkpoint image.
Compatibility annotations preserve source image, Podman, CRIU, OCI runtime, conmon, architecture, kernel, cgroup, and distribution context.
Restore fails on several topology and runtime incompatibilities instead of silently representing every import as success.
known_limits: The OCI manifest identifies the outer config and layer blobs, not an itemized per-entry manifest for every checkpoint entry inside the layer.
Checkpoint-image import copies a fixed entry set and logs unavailable entries rather than producing a signed, exact inventory acknowledgment.
Restore performs only a minimal CRIU inventory.img existence check before deeper restore.
The original rootfs image is pulled by name if missing, so the checkpoint image is not a hidden-predecessor-state-free package.
Compatible runtime, CRIU, kernel, cgroup, storage, network, and volume conditions remain external dependencies.
The exact checkpoint-image test observes running state for a top workload but not application-specific output continuity, semantic correctness, or data-plane service behavior.
The stronger cross-root timestamp and volume continuation receipt uses the export/import archive path, not the exact OCI checkpoint image, and cannot be borrowed into this control.
Same-project code, tests, and review are not external independent reproduction.
The control proves a system package-to-operation join and does not establish person-level operator capability.

controls.public_label: cross-root checkpoint archive with service, output, and volume continuation

source_records.title: Checkpoint and restore system test with cross-root service continuation
source_records.artifact_scope: Exports a checkpoint archive from a unique Podman root, restores it into the regular root, verifies the web service, observes timestamp growth, and checks volume content transfer.

source_records.title: Checkpoint archive export contract
source_records.artifact_scope: Defines exported checkpoint archives, rootfs and volume inclusion, compression, TCP and file-lock choices, and migration intent.

source_records.title: Checkpoint archive import contract
source_records.artifact_scope: Defines import from another host or root, runtime selection, volume and rootfs controls, static network handling, and restore options.

source_records.title: Checkpoint archive inventory construction and restore path
source_records.artifact_scope: Serializes CRIU state, config/spec, network, rootfs differences, shared memory, logs, and named volumes into the export archive and restores selected entries.

components.same_object_identity: The exported container configuration and checkpoint state are imported into a different Podman storage root and restored as the same named service object.
components.package_identity: One checkpoint tar archive carries CRIU images, config/spec, network state, rootfs changes, shared memory, and volume archives.
components.package_content_addressing: The command surface does not create or require one OCI manifest or package digest for the exported tar archive.
components.internal_inventory_and_entry_integrity: A known implementation list determines archive entries, but the archive lacks a public itemized per-entry checksum manifest acknowledged at import.
components.outgoing_and_incoming_roles: The source Podman root exports the archive and the destination Podman root imports and restores it.
components.authority_and_credentials: Container configuration and port state travel, but complete authority, credential, secret, and recipient-rights custody is not separately itemized.
components.dependencies_and_access: The destination still requires compatible runtime, CRIU, kernel, cgroups, storage, base rootfs image availability, and appropriate network and volume conditions.
components.open_decisions_and_deadlines: Rootfs, volume, name, TCP, network, pod, and port choices remain restore invocation parameters rather than acknowledged package state.
components.rollback_safe_decline_and_failure_contai: Restore can fail on runtime, volume, topology, or checkpoint incompatibility, but the test does not bind one package-level rollback or safe-decline receipt.
components.recipient_or_successor_acknowledgment: The destination root successfully imports and runs the service, but does not sign or enumerate an exact archive inventory and dependency ledger.
components.successor_operation_from_package: After import, the web service responds, its timestamp file advances, and transferred volume content remains available.
components.independent_verification: The cross-root receipt is a same-project system test, not an external independent reproduction.

positive_findings: The source and destination use different Podman storage roots.
The original container is checkpointed and exported before the destination imports the archive.
The restored web service responds after import.
Application output advances after restore rather than merely reporting a running state.
Named-volume content is present after transfer.
Runtime mismatch and several incompatible restore conditions can fail closed.
known_limits: The exported tar archive has no required content-addressed OCI manifest or package digest in the cited receipt.
The archive lacks a recipient-acknowledged itemized per-entry integrity ledger.
The destination depends on compatible software, kernel, runtime, CRIU, storage, network, and base-image state.
The test preconditions and destination environment are controlled by the originating project.
No complete authority, credential, open-decision, or rollback ledger is acknowledged.
Same-project system testing is not external independent review.
This stronger application-specific continuation cannot be combined with the separate OCI checkpoint-image digest surface to claim one exact package.

controls.public_label: same-PID live-process handoff without portable package custody

source_records.title: Live-upgrade envd inside a running sandbox at resume
source_records.artifact_scope: Defines same-PID process-image replacement, carried state, failure handling, version confirmation, and one-hop and two-hop workload continuation.

source_records.title: envd process handover implementation
source_records.artifact_scope: Serializes state, relocates descriptors, executes the successor image, re-adopts processes, and restores retained exits.

source_records.title: envd handover state schema
source_records.artifact_scope: Makes process, descriptor, timeout, terminal-event, watcher, mount, and forwarding state addressable across the binary transition.

source_records.title: documented envd live-upgrade architecture
source_records.artifact_scope: Documents the authenticated endpoint, same-PID responsibility transfer, resume ordering, and operational boundaries.

components.same_object_identity: The same running sandbox workload and envd parent cross one same-PID process-image transition.
components.package_identity: A streamed successor binary and tmpfs handover JSON exist, but no one portable package joins both.
components.package_content_addressing: Version gates and fixed paths exist without one package-level manifest and exact digest binding the transferred binary and state.
components.internal_inventory_and_entry_integrity: Process, descriptor, timeout, watcher, terminal, mount, and forwarding state is typed, but not exported as a recipient-acknowledged portable inventory.
components.outgoing_and_incoming_roles: Outgoing envd serializes state and incoming --resume-handover envd re-adopts it after syscall.Exec.
components.authority_and_credentials: The endpoint is authenticated and version-gated; a portable authority and credential ledger is absent.
components.dependencies_and_access: The transition depends on the same sandbox, fixed binary path, runtime, descriptors, mounts, and originating control plane.
components.open_decisions_and_deadlines: Remaining timeouts and target-version choices are carried, not a complete portable decision and deadline inventory.
components.rollback_safe_decline_and_failure_contai: Pre-exec failure can retain and thaw the old envd; unrecoverable post-exec failure tears down rather than representing partial success.
components.recipient_or_successor_acknowledgment: The successor re-adopts state and confirms the running version, not an itemized portable package inventory.
components.successor_operation_from_package: The same workload PID continues and produces additional output across one-hop and two-hop process-image replacements.
components.independent_verification: Public tests and multi-reviewer repair remain inside the originating project.

positive_findings: The same workload PID continues across process-image replacement.
Application output increases after handoff.
A two-hop version chain preserves the workload.
Version confirmation separates transport failure from successful upgrade.
Failure paths distinguish recoverable pre-exec from unrecoverable post-exec states.
known_limits: The binary and handover state are not one portable content-addressed package.
No recipient inventory acknowledgment exists.
The transition depends on the originating sandbox and control plane.
One system-process quiescence edge remains.
Same-project tests are not external independent review.
System continuity is not person-level operator evidence.

controls.public_label: complete content-bound proof package without operational successor
controls.system_or_subject: Cargo OS PDS portable Proof of Handover

source_records.title: Bind portable Proof of Handover artifacts
source_records.artifact_scope: Binds responsibility transfer, audit lineage, Evidence Bundle, Policy, and Verification Certificate into one deterministic root.

source_records.title: Require both Proof of Handover participant signatures
source_records.artifact_scope: Requires trusted outgoing and incoming participant signatures over the same binding root.

source_records.title: Verify complete portable Proof of Handover
source_records.artifact_scope: Recalculates the Bundle signature, trusted timestamp, decision certificate, transfer, audit lineage, and both participant signatures.

source_records.title: portable Proof of Handover verification implementation
source_records.artifact_scope: Implements canonical-order proof recalculation and substitution rejection.

components.same_object_identity: One responsibility-transfer proof object is identified; no live workload object crosses into successor operation.
components.package_identity: Transfer, audit lineage, Evidence Bundle, Policy, certificate, and signatures are bound into one portable proof structure.
components.package_content_addressing: Deterministic roots, signatures, timestamp, and certificate content-bind the proof package.
components.internal_inventory_and_entry_integrity: The proof components are bound and recalculated, but the object does not enumerate a live operational inventory of runtime state, dependencies, credentials, and access.
components.outgoing_and_incoming_roles: Outgoing and incoming participants are explicit proof signers, not observed runtime operators.
components.authority_and_credentials: Key identity, validity, revocation, signing time, and participant role are checked at proof scope.
components.dependencies_and_access: Proof dependencies are bound; operational runtime dependencies and access state are outside the object.
components.open_decisions_and_deadlines: The Policy decision is replayed; live operational decisions and deadlines are absent.
components.rollback_safe_decline_and_failure_contai: Modified proof layers and invalid trust state fail closed.
components.recipient_or_successor_acknowledgment: The incoming participant signs the proof root, not an itemized operational package inventory.
components.successor_operation_from_package: No live successor operation is observed and physical actuation remains out of scope.
components.independent_verification: The same system recalculates the proof; no external institution reproduces live operation.

positive_findings: Every proof component binds to one deterministic root.
Outgoing and incoming participants sign the same proof.
The proof is recalculated from supplied artifacts.
Audit, manifest, and signature substitutions fail closed.
known_limits: The proof object is not an operational runtime-state package.
The incoming signature is not an itemized operational inventory receipt.
No successor operates a live object from the proof.
Operational dependencies, access, credentials, and rollback state are absent.
Same-project recalculation is not external independent review.
Proof completion is not person-level operator evidence.

next_action: Seek one exact checkpoint package whose internal entries, base image or rootfs, runtime and kernel dependencies, credentials and authority, network and volume access, open decisions, and rollback state are itemized and integrity-bound; whose recipient acknowledges that inventory; whose destination begins clean without hidden predecessor state; whose application-specific continuation is observed; and whose whole chain is independently reproduced outside the originating project. Do not borrow Podman export/import service continuity into the OCI image case, combine E2B live continuity with Cargo proof, or convert a system control into person support.
